options.text: By incomplete combustion of fossil fuels when oxygen supply is limited
By complete combustion of fossil fuels
By plants during photosynthesis
By dissolving carbon dioxide in water

questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is produced by the incomplete combustion of fossil fuels, which occurs when there is not enough oxygen for complete combustion. It is a colourless, odourless, toxic gas.

questions.stem: Why is carbon monoxide dangerous to humans?

options.text: It binds to haemoglobin in red blood cells, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen
It causes global warming
It dissolves the ozone layer
It causes acid rain

questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin in red blood cells more strongly than oxygen does. This reduces the amount of oxygen the blood can carry, which can be fatal at high concentrations.

questions.stem: What are the main pollutants produced by burning fossil fuels in vehicle engines?

options.text: Oxygen and nitrogen
Carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, and particulates
Hydrogen and helium
Only water vapour

questions.explanation: Burning fossil fuels produces carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide (from incomplete combustion), sulfur dioxide (from sulfur impurities), nitrogen oxides (from high-temperature reactions with atmospheric nitrogen), and particulates (soot).

questions.stem: How are nitrogen oxides (NOx) formed in car engines?

options.text: From the catalytic converter
By mixing nitrogen with water
When nitrogen and oxygen from the air react at the high temperatures inside the engine
From nitrogen impurities in the fuel

questions.explanation: At the very high temperatures inside a car engine, nitrogen and oxygen from the air react together to form nitrogen oxides. These pollutants contribute to acid rain and photochemical smog.

questions.stem: What do particulates (soot) cause when released into the atmosphere?

options.text: They have no harmful effects
They increase oxygen levels in the air
They make the air smell pleasant
They cause respiratory problems and can worsen conditions like asthma; they also contribute to global dimming

questions.explanation: Particulates (tiny solid particles) cause respiratory problems, worsen asthma and other lung conditions, and contribute to global dimming by reducing the amount of sunlight reaching the Earth's surface.

questions.stem: How does a catalytic converter reduce pollution from car exhausts?

options.text: It filters out all gases and only releases oxygen
It burns the exhaust gases at high temperature
It dissolves the pollutants in water
It converts carbon monoxide into carbon dioxide and nitrogen oxides into nitrogen, using a platinum/rhodium catalyst

questions.explanation: A catalytic converter uses platinum and rhodium catalysts to convert toxic carbon monoxide into less harmful carbon dioxide, and nitrogen oxides back into nitrogen and oxygen.

questions.stem: Where does the sulfur dioxide in air pollution mainly come from?

options.text: From nitrogen in the air reacting with water
From sulfur impurities in fossil fuels burning during combustion
From plants releasing sulfur during photosynthesis
From the ozone layer breaking down

questions.explanation: Sulfur dioxide is produced when sulfur impurities in fossil fuels (especially coal and diesel) burn during combustion. It is a major contributor to acid rain.
